purpose: Controlled vocabulary for Landscape Interpretation Engine stories. Labels teach reading landscapes; they are not classification outputs.
languageNotes: Prefer interpretive phrasing: may, suggests, consistent with, possible remnant of.
Do not present taxonomy labels as confirmed land history without supporting evidence.
Regional applicability varies — Northeast US pasture walls differ from western fencing cues.

categories.label: Land Use History
categories.description: Human land-use legacies that still shape vegetation, soils, and structure.

terms.label: Former pasture
terms.notes: Often stones, barbed wire remnants, even-aged tree lines along walls.

terms.label: Former hay field
terms.notes: Open canopy invasions, linear edges, fewer wall corridors than pasture.

terms.label: Historic orchard
terms.notes: Grid spacing, grafted stock, volunteer fruit trees.

terms.label: Old homestead
terms.notes: Foundation stones, cellar holes, lilac/rhododendron clumps, metal debris.

terms.label: Logging history
terms.notes: Stumps, skid trails, even-aged cohorts, landing scars.

terms.label: Abandoned road
terms.notes: Parallel berms, compacted soils, mid-succession corridors.

terms.label: Stone wall boundary
terms.notes: Property or pasture divisions; walls alone do not prove pasture.

terms.label: Historic charcoal production
terms.notes: Circular charcoal pits, dark soils, nearby ore/iron contexts in some regions.

terms.label: Mining influence
terms.notes: Spoil, prospect pits, adits — use extreme caution and legal/safety notes.

categories.label: Forest Development
categories.description: Stand age, structure, and successional stage relative to disturbance.

terms.label: Young forest
terms.notes: Dense stems, limited understory differentiation.

terms.label: Even-aged forest
terms.notes: Cohort canopy from shared disturbance or planting.

terms.label: Mature forest
terms.notes: Larger diameters, canopy closure, developing vertical structure.

terms.label: Old-growth indicators
terms.notes: Indicators only — not an official designation claim.

terms.label: Early succession
terms.notes: Herb/shrub/pioneer tree dominance after opening.

terms.label: Mid succession
terms.notes: Closing canopy; competition among mid-tolerant species.

terms.label: Late succession
terms.notes: Shade-tolerant regeneration, complex deadwood.

terms.label: Canopy gap dynamics
terms.notes: Localized openings from windthrow, mortality, or harvest.

categories.label: Water Processes
categories.description: Hydrologic and wetland processes written into form and vegetation.

terms.label: Floodplain
terms.notes: Flat valley bottoms subject to overbank flow.

terms.label: Seasonal wetland
terms.notes: Wet-dry cycles; vernal pools may be a subclass later.

terms.label: Spring seep
terms.notes: Groundwater discharge; often indicator plants and soft ground.

terms.label: Beaver influence
terms.notes: Dams, lodges, drowned timber, meadow creation/abandonment cycles.

terms.label: River terrace
terms.notes: Abandoned flood levels above the active channel.

terms.label: Oxbow
terms.notes: Cutoff meander lakes or wet depressions.

terms.label: Headwaters
terms.notes: First-order streams; sensitive cold-water habitat.

terms.label: Riparian corridor
terms.notes: Stream-adjacent vegetation structure distinct from upland.

categories.label: Geological Processes
categories.description: Landforms and materials from ice, rock, and long time.

terms.label: Glacial deposits
terms.notes: Till and outwash mosaics; regional textbooks first.

terms.label: Moraine
terms.notes: Ice-margin ridges and unsorted debris.

terms.label: Esker
terms.notes: Sinuous sand/gravel ridges from meltwater tunnels.

terms.label: Kettle
terms.notes: Closed depressions from buried ice melt.

terms.label: Talus slope
terms.notes: Angular rock below cliffs.

terms.label: Ancient shoreline
terms.notes: Strandlines from former lakes/seas.

terms.label: Bedrock exposure
terms.notes: Outcrops; useful for thin soils and acid communities.

terms.label: Karst
terms.notes: Future — sinkholes, springs in carbonate terranes; regional only.

categories.label: Habitat Structure
categories.description: Present-day arrangement of cover, edges, and composition.

terms.label: Edge habitat
terms.notes: Transitions with high structural contrast.

terms.label: Interior forest
terms.notes: Away from abrupt openings; microclimate cooler/moister.

terms.label: Shrubland
terms.notes: Persistent or early-mid shrub dominance.

terms.label: Meadow succession
terms.notes: Grass/forb openings moving toward woody cover.

terms.label: Conifer transition
terms.notes: Increasing conifer share or plantation edges.

terms.label: Hardwood dominance
terms.notes: Broadleaf canopy character.

terms.label: Mixed forest
terms.notes: Conifer and hardwood canopy together.
